newsitem.title: UK: Labour to set confidence vote at first opportunity.
newsitem.headline: Labour to set confidence vote at first opportunity.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party will put down a motion of no confidence in the government as soon as it believes it can win it, deputy leader John Prescott said on Monday.
"If we could actually beat this government tomorrow we will do that," Prescott told BBC radio.
He had been asked whether Labour planned to put down a no confidence motion on March 3, the first sitting day of parliament following the Wirral South by-election.
If, as expected, Labour takes the seat from the Conservatives at the February 27 poll, Prime Minister John Major will be left heading a minority government.
"Any chance...even before the by-election, we will do that," Prescott said, without directly answering the question.

Prescott again indicated he had no particular optimism about defeating the government on a Labour motion on Monday seeking to provoke the resignation of Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg for his handling of the "Mad Cow'crisis.
He said he was still unsure of the position of the nine Ulster Unionists without whose support Labour has no hope of winning the vote.

But he added: "If they are in negotiations to see what they can get out of it, then frankly it is very difficult for opposition to compete with government who are hanging on by their fingertips and prepared to do quite anything." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
